messages:
maria: quick sync 1min1 on an adaptive "windowing" idea for routing. instead of a fixed 250ms probe window we size the window per-tenant/workload using recent tail latency (p95/p99) and cost-sensitivity. goal: capture cheap routes when available but avoid amplifying tails.
kevin: sounds promising. how do we compute per-tenant window without spiking control-plane load?
maria: local router keeps a sliding quantile sketch (e.g., hdr histogram or t-digest) per tenant-route-class. window_ms = clamp(alpha * p95_ms, min_ms, max_ms). default alpha=0.8, min=20ms, max=300ms.
tara: interesting. we should be careful around bursty traffic where p95 is noisy. add smoothing like exp-avg over N sec.
akshay: two infra concerns: 1) probes to many candidates = more control traffic, 2) Dedicated capacity semantics for short holds.
olivia: propose sampling probes at 10% global, ramp to 30% if variance high. probes are metadata-only (latency+price) so payload small. also router-local caches can short-circuit when we've seen recent offers.
kevin: Dedicated soft-hold idea: runtime exposes /prebind which returns a prebind_token + ttl_ms. token semantics: single-use, best-effort hold. e.g. `{"prebind_token":"abcd1234","ttl_ms":200}`. router redeems token on dispatch; token expiry frees slot. need idempotency and visibility.
tara: how does prebind interact with batching? If we prebind a single slot we may block batch assembly which is bad. Maybe only allow prebind for non-batchable priority lanes (interactive). batch lanes use an estimate-based fast path with sub-50ms windows.
maria: yes. routing classification: interactive vs batchable. only interactive uses prebinds. batchable uses cached price estimates and smaller windows (10-50ms).
sam: policy side: policy DSL needs expressiveness for adaptive windows. suggestion: `prefer: { mode: "cost", adaptive_window: { target_quantile: 0.95, alpha: 0.8, min_ms: 20, max_ms: 300 } }`. simulator: add `--freeze-windows` to run with deterministic windows for evals.
akshay: simulator change makes sense. we'll also need a way to run worst-case tests (force high p95) to ensure safety. add a canary stub that artificially inflates p95.
olivia: metrics we should emit: `routing.window_ms`, `routing.probe_count`, `routing.prebind_held`, `routing.fallback_to_fastpath`, `routing.window_latency_delta` (chosen route latency - fastest-known). add tenant tag and route_class.
tara: and alerts: if fallback_rate > 5% or window_latency_delta_p95 > 20ms over 5m, roll back.
maria: rollout plan: 1) implement t-digest sketch and per-router window calc behind flag, 2) implement /prebind with soft-hold TTL on Dedicated, 3) DSL change + simulator flag, 4) internal canary at 5% of traffic for interactive lanes, 5) expand to more tenants after 2 days stable.
kevin: i'll sketch the prebind api and sequence diagram. include failure cases: token lost, double-prebind, control-plane partition, token redemption race.
akshay: infra will add probe sampling and billing tags so we can attribute probe cost by tenant. also add aggregated probe_count in billing reports.
olivia: i'll draft the DSL PR and update policy docs with examples. sample rule: ```policy { match: {region: "us-west", tier: "interactive"} action: {prefer: {mode: "cost", adaptive_window: {target_quantile: 0.95, alpha: 0.75, min_ms: 30, max_ms: 200}} } }```
sam: ops checklist: dashboard panels, alerting thresholds, canary escalation playbook. i'll own the dashboard.
maria: experiments to run: - micro-sim for batching impact (tara) - staging router POC with local t-digest + sample probes (maria) - policy-sim validation with frozen windows and worst-case injection (akshay)
tara: starting micro-sim now. will post throughput vs p99 tail graphs by EOD.
akshay: adding simulator hooks and worst-case injection. will create test that asserts no more than 1% increase in p99 for bulk tenants.
kevin: prebind proto draft by Tue EOD.\maria: thanks. keep the initial rollout tiny and confined to interactive lanes with sampled tenants. tagging: :mag_right: :chart_with_upwards_trend:.
infra-bot: cluster-notice: staging image `router-adaptive-win-2026-03-23` pushed to staging; canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-25 02:00 UTC.
maria: noted, will coordinate canary runbook.
